answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it votes on shared work. A Sybil attacker must split real capital across many identities; if those identities endorse fabricated results, a challenge backed by reproducible evidence can slash their stake, while honest reviewers recover theirs. The rule does not prove one person equals one identity, but makes fake influence costly and risky. A reef of independent checks, a ferrous bond, and a public beacon for disputes make mass deception harder to sustain.
